decision: the image carries an instruction-set map: sorted (address, A32 or Thumb) transitions, the same shape as ELF mapping symbols
why: an armhf binary mixes A32 (.plt, .init, crti) and Thumb; the mode of a byte is a property of the image, and the decoder must know it at every seek
evidence: target/probe readelf: 27 $a and 266 $t in armhf ls

decision: map comes from $a/$t symbols when .symtab survives, else from a pre-pass at load that follows B/BL/BLX from seeds whose mode is known (entry, exports, relocated pointers with the Thumb bit, DT_INIT/DT_FINI, .plt as A32)
why: Debian and most firmware binaries are stripped; the Thumb bit on every pointer the loader sees is the mode evidence ARM itself uses

decision: Arch::decode and Arch::decoder take the image, in a behavior-preserving commit of its own
why: the alternatives (mode in an address bit, thread-local map, two address views) push the mode into every consumer of an address; one parameter keeps it inside the arch

decision: the Arm arch reuses thumb.rs decoding and register State; A32 adds its own decoder that writes the same State

decision: truth from the dbgsym debug file: functions from FUNC symbols minus the Thumb bit, instructions decoded by yaxpeax-arm in the mode the $a/$t symbols give, jump tables from $d runs after a dispatch and from A32 branch tables

decision: ARM truth from dbgsym files: functions, calls via A32 PLT, five switch dispatch forms (TBB/TBH, ADD PC,PC table in .rodata, row of branches, LDR PC table, clang ADD PC,Rt,Re); a table counts only if every case is an instruction of its function
